NEW METHOD NOTE (C-1200-A, self-corrected before publishing): C-1199 recorded "trades max id 2272 unchanged since C-1198, 0 new rows" as a finding. That reading is an artefact of the rolling 500-row page, not a fact about the system: /api/trades?limit=500 is a sliding window (oldest id drifts forward every control: 1773 -> 1775 between C-1199 and C-1200) and the page sorts by `timestamp DESC, id ASC` while `timestamp` is the CYCLE time. A whole-set id diff is the only valid comparison: C-1199 -> C-1200 added ids 2273/2274 (the two swing entries) and aged out 1773/1774. Also: the trade row's gross/fee/net fields are `gross`, `fee`, `net` - a lookup for `gross_pl`/`fees`/`net_pl` returns 0/500 non-null and reads as "accounting absent" when 161/500 rows in fact carry a fifo-lot-matched gross.

**NEW FINDING C-1141-B (method, reliability/observability, NOT changed): the run log carries THREE timestamps, and a blackout's own boundary row is back-dated.** `timestamp` == `created_at` == the row's WRITE time, and `duration_ms` is measured from cycle start, so a cycle that COMPLETES late writes a row whose write time equals its dispatch time and whose `duration_ms` overstates its own runtime - the missing interval sits BEFORE the row, not inside it. Evidence: row 21589 (reconcile) has created_at 18:20:28 and duration_ms 6,204, i.e. it ran 18:20:22-18:20:28, so the 90-minute gap ENDS at ~18:20:22, not at 18:20:21.5 (reconstructed dispatch) and certainly not at 18:20:28. The C-1130-A reconstruction (`created_at - duration_ms`) is still the right way to find WHICH scheduled slot a row belongs to, but it must never be used as a blackout ENDPOINT - it moves the boundary 90-310 minutes the wrong way. Gap durations must be read from created_at to created_at.

## Control-976 (Sep 30 09:08+02 / 07:08 UTC Wed) - strict read-only control + **CORRECTION of a four-control documentation defect (swing-fire DOW mapping)**: Alpaca HEALTHY in all live respects; occ-27 stands (not cleared); **the "Sep 29 22:00z DOW=2 swing fire never ran" claim repeated by Controls 968/970/972/974 is CORRECT ON THE FACTS BUT MISLABELLED ON THE CONVENTION**, NO deploy, no code/config/cap change, docs-only update.

**Method correction (the substance of this control).** Controls 968/970/972/974 labelled the missed Sep 29 22:00z swing fire "DOW=2" and described the miss as an unexplained durable condition. Two things are wrong with that framing, and one thing is right.

*Right:* the fire WAS expected and DID NOT RUN. `0 22 * * 2-6` with Cloudflare's `1=Sunday` convention (documented in this runbook's reference header and in README) means Mon-Fri inclusive of Tuesday. Cloudflare's own cron reference states that when both day-of-month and day-of-week are restricted the job runs when *either* matches, which for `0 22 * * 2-6` fires every day (day-of-month `*`), so the Tuesday 22:00z slot is unambiguously scheduled. The expression in the live registration is unchanged and CF-verified: `('0 22 * * 2-6', modified_on 2026-09-28T20:04:34.219701Z)`.

*Wrong (label):* Sep 29 is a **Tuesday**, and Tuesday under `1=Sunday` is **DOW=3**, not DOW=2. The four controls used the python `weekday()` value (Mon=0) as if it were the CF DOW value. The same documents use CF DOW correctly everywhere else - Sep 14 Mon = DOW=2, Sep 15 Tue = DOW=3, Sep 16 Wed = DOW=4, Sep 17 Thu = DOW=5, Sep 24 Thu = "DOW=4 cadence test" - so the docs now contain two mutually contradictory conventions, which will mislead the next control that has to decide whether a missing fire is expected.

*Wrong (durability framing):* the missed Tuesday fire is NOT evidence of a new durable defect. It falls **inside occ-27's suppression window**, which this control re-confirms as the only time-gap in the whole run log: the sole gap >10 min across 500 rows is 19050 `2026-09-29 18:41:01z` -> 19051 `2026-09-30 00:01:12z` = **320.2 min, all-trigger**, covering the 22:00z slot. So the swing miss is a *consequence of the same suppression event* (dispatch was dead for 5h20m through 00:01z), not a separate/durable swing condition. Labelling it a fourth "no self-heal" confirmation of an independent defect inflates occ-27 into two findings.

**Consequence for the next swing fire - and a NEW escalation-relevant fact.** Because occ-27's window swallowed the Tue Sep 29 fire, **the Wed Sep 30 22:00z fire (CF DOW=4) is the first scheduled opportunity since Sep 28 and therefore becomes the real test of whether swing dispatch still works at all**. One datapoint that argues against alarm: the last swing fire (Sep 28 22:01:18z, run 18635) ran **inside** the occ-27 window's tail end at a minute when reconcile had already stalled (reconcile rows stop at 18:41:01z and do not resume until 00:01:12z, yet the 22:01:18z swing run exists). Dispatch was demonstrably still able to deliver *some* triggers at 22:01z; the Tue slot got nothing. That asymmetry is now the open question for tonight.

**Live state (healthy; no deploy warranted).** 8 routes x 2 probes all HTTP 200, zero `D1_ERROR` - Sep 29's D1 free-tier read-limit exhaustion stays CLEARED. Equity **$97,140.84 POSITIVE**, last_equity $97,111.1145, day +$29.73, **~$141 above the $97,000 floor** (never touched). Run log 500/500 rows id-contiguous 18695->19194, **zero id gaps**, zero `CYCLE_LEASE_HELD`, zero suppression other than occ-27. Today (Sep 30 00:00z-07:07z): daytrading **86/86 intended 5-min slots present, zero missing**; reconcile 43 rows, **42/42 consecutive deltas exactly 10.0 min**; crypto 15/15 at exactly `:07`/`:37`, all `CRYPTO_DISABLED_BY_CONFIG` fail-closed. 7 error-class runs, all pre-existing Sep 29 `POSITION_QTY_MISMATCH` (fail-safe held: broker-authoritative quantity persisted, new entries blocked that cycle). Positions 22 (source alpaca, positionsAvailable true): 15 swing-tagged cost **$3,647.88** / MV $3,361.47, 5 daytrading cost **$4,759.89 < $5,000**, 2 unattributed MS+RUN **$246.82**. Trades 100/100 filled, 0/100 carry fee or net, all `fee_attribution` = `none-recorded` (aggregate-only, conservatively unattributed); accounting 72 `filled_lot_exact_unavailable` / 28 `fifo-lot-matched`. Caps 5000/3700/2000, guards 150/100/100/97000, `min_confidence` 0.8, `crypto_trading_enabled` false, `eod_flatten` true - all unchanged. `/health` 2.8.2 ok; `/api/config` `version` still reads the known cosmetic 2.7.0 D1-seed lag (not a defect). 281 tests / 1016 assertions PASS, `bunx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

**Finding C-950-A: INVESTIGATED AND REFUTED - the equity-direction fallback is unit-correct; no defect, no deploy.** Mid-sweep, a suspected defect was raised: that `resolveEquityDirection` (`src/equity-observability.ts`) writes the raw DOLLAR equity delta into `change_today_pct` and the legacy daily-loss guards (`src/risk-manager.ts:164` limit 15, `src/swing-risk.ts:142` limit 5, both documented as percent points with a 1-50 validation range at `risk-manager.ts:490`) read it as percent, spuriously halting new entries at a -$5/-$15 daily loss instead of the intended ~$4,856/$14,567. **Refuted on the evidence:** (1) the source at HEAD `a6806ec` and in the live bundle returns `changeTodayPct: (delta / lastEquity) * 100` - correct percent points - and `git log --follow` shows no later change, so the correct formula has been in place since the file's introduction (commit `20d80ac`); (2) the production run that triggered the suspicion (run 19048, 18:37:08z) logs `fallback_change_today_pct: -0.018735754494917045` - the CORRECT percent for the observed pair (equity 97092.92, last_equity 97111.1145) - while `change_today_pct: 0` in the same context is the raw BROKER value logged before the overwrite, by design; (3) the alarming "-18.1945" figure was the investigator's own arithmetic of the raw delta, never an observed production value. The apparent `EQUITY_DIRECTION_FALLBACK` volume (102 runs today: 62 daytrading-cron + 40 crypto) is the fallback OBSERVED and CORRECT, firing whenever the broker reports a 0 daily percent, and its computed percent is right every time it was checked. An independent adversarial subagent review reached the same refutation. **Process lesson recorded: a unit-mismatch claim must be confirmed against an OBSERVED production value of the suspected wrong-unit field before any code change or deploy - deriving the wrong-unit value by hand from correct-looking context keys manufactures a defect that is not there.** The value delivered by this false alarm: two regression tests pinning the correct percent convention (production pair 97092.92/97111.1145 must yield changeToday -18.1945 dollars AND changeTodayPct -0.01873575 percent, plus a broker-percent parity case), and the consuming-unit clarification now lives in the test comments rather than the shipped source, keeping the bundle byte-identical to live.

## Release 2.8.0 (Sep 19 09:45 +02 / 07:45 UTC Sat Sep 19): **TRADING ANALYTICS & REVIEW — new dashboard section + A4 reports (deployed, Joachim-requested feature)** - release 2.8.0 (bundle md5 **2664cfec8bf746829f14d3f5d0f6eec5**, 357,050 B, RELEASE_VERSION 2.8.0), 261 tests / 956 assertions PASS (18 new analytics tests), typecheck 0. **New:** (1) `src/analytics.ts` — deterministic Trading-Analytics engine computing per-closed-trade analysis from stored D1 data only: Decision Quality scored from ENTRY-TIME information exclusively (TA snapshot emaTrend/macdTrend/adx/volumeRatio/rsi/pricePosition/vwapDeviation + confidence + planned R:R from intent stop/target; realized outcome NEVER enters the score — no hindsight/outcome bias; labels Strong/Good/Questionable/Weak + internal 0-100 score), Execution Quality (slippage = |fill - price_at_decision| vs ATR tolerance), Trade Management (planned-envelope adherence proxy), Exit Quality (close_reason semantics), Outcome (P/L, P/L %, realized R from stored stop × qty, initial risk in USD), acceptable-vs-avoidable loss classification (Strong/Good + compliant + slippage-within-ATR = acceptable), whatWorked/whatCouldImprove/learningPoint generated from concrete findings only, MFE/MAE/funding/leverage explicitly null ("Insufficient data" in UI) because the broker integration does not record them — NOTHING fabricated. (2) `GET /api/analytics` — strictly read-only, period (7/30/90/YTD/all/custom), filters (strategy, symbol, side, result, regime, confidence band); returns KPIs (net P/L, win rate, profit factor, expectancy + expectancy-in-R, avg win/loss, avg planned R:R, max drawdown, avg duration, attributed fees, long/short split, avg decision quality, avg realized R), cumulative P/L + drawdown curves, confidence calibration (5 bands) with explicit miscalibration verdict, combination pattern analysis (side × regime × volatility × confidence-band, n>=3, evidence Preliminary/Moderate/Strong by sample size, chronological 60/40 out-of-sample check), winner/loser top/bottom 20%, day-vs-swing comparison across risk/consistency/expectancy/drawdown/costs/duration/result-volatility (no simplistic "best" verdict), research backlog (Title/Observation/Evidence/Sample size/Hypothesis/Proposed test/Success criteria/Status=New — hypotheses to backtest, never direct strategy changes), robustness block with chronological split. (3) Dashboard "Analytics" tab — same design tokens/components, period buttons + custom dates, filters, KPI grid, cumulative P/L + drawdown charts, calibration table, patterns (What Works / Needs Attention), day-vs-swing comparison, research backlog, trade-by-trade analysis with per-trade detail (market context, ORIGINAL AI thesis unchanged, entry/execution/management/exit review, outcome, data gaps). (4) A4 reports — Export Day/Swing Trading Report buttons build a one-page A4 portrait sheet (header, 6-8 KPIs, cumulative P/L main graph, max 3 What Works + 3 Improvements, 3-5 line Trading Review; priority-ordered content so it can NEVER exceed one page; black/white-safe with symbols not color-only) and open the print dialog for Save-as-PDF. (5) `analytics_snapshots` D1 table + daily watermark-gated snapshot write in scheduled maintenance (`last_analytics_snapshot_date` config, ONCE/day, idempotent upsert) so improvement over time is measurable; table also created idempotently by the writer (analytics-snapshots-migration.sql for fresh installs). Original AI thesis (decisions.reason/ai_reasoning) is never rewritten; post-trade review text is a separate field. Caps/guards/min_confidence 0.8 UNTOUCHED by this release.
